wwo.name: Kyoto
wwo.method: The 1889 survey connects Shijo Karasuma and Nishiki to the Kamo crossing, Gion and the early Maruyama park, and links upper Karasuma to the Nishijin textile blocks. The southern survey mosaic traces Shijo to the Honganji blocks and the late Meiji rail and village fringe at Toji. Individual ordinary parcels and minor widths are inferred. Untraced streets keep the fallback.

registration.reference: Affine registration against four matched tiles of a georeferenced copy of the same 1892 edition. Intermediate pixels are Web Mercator z16. GeoJSON is CRS84.
registration.precision_limit: Fit residual applies only within the overlap. The central and western parts of the corridor use affine extrapolation. The fit is to another copy of the map. Positional and apparent construction dimensions are approximate. Nishijin and the Karasuma connector use the same edition on additional scan crops west and north of the overlap. The affine residual is not a measured error for these additions.

toji.method: Direct z16 coordinate recovery from the georeferenced historical survey mosaic. Pixel origin [14714624,6644992]. The new Karasuma approach joins the southernmost end of the existing surveyed centerline, approximately 8 m from the corresponding alignment in this mosaic.
toji.precision: The ARC mosaic is a map registration, not a current cadastral survey. Near Shijo, registration is compared with the existing trace of the same edition. Southern links are interpreted only where line and hatching can be read.

sources.title: Imperial Land Survey provisional sheets of Kyoto, Shijo to Toji

sources.precision: Read from the Meiji mid-period tiles, z16 global pixels x 57479–57482 and y 25957–25963. Hatching and linework constrain blocks and roads. The existing Shijo survey alignment overlaps. No sub-block absolute survey accuracy, frontage depth, or later track geometry is implied.

sources.title: Toji and Rokkusonno landscape study, 1892 survey
sources.licence: Historical geography reference. No scan or document media redistributed.

sources.title: Locating the first Kyoto station

sources.licence: Historical reference. No document media redistributed.
sources.precision: Identifies the first station south of Shiokoji between Higashinotoin and Karasuma, and distinguishes it from the 1914 relocation. Used to date the mapped rail fringe.
